Strike Ends at Key Chinese Industrial Intermediate Producer, Output Resumes

A week-long strike at Jinxiang Industrial Materials Co., a leading Chinese manufacturer of industrial intermediate products, ended on Monday following a new wage agreement reached between workers and management. The labor action, which began on May 27 at the company’s main facility in Shandong Province, had brought production to a standstill, disrupting supply lines for several major contracts.

Jinxiang Industrial Materials is a core supplier of specialty chemicals and processed metals used in the fabrication of industrial components. According to the Shandong Industrial Association, the strike prevented the shipment of more than 9,000 metric tons of intermediate goods, resulting in an estimated 7% reduction in the company’s monthly output.

Workers at Jinxiang’s primary plant staged a walkout after contract negotiations broke down over wage increases and overtime pay. The Jinxiang Workers’ Union said its members had not received a meaningful pay rise in three years despite rising living costs. "We had no choice but to make our voices heard," said union chairman Li Qiang. "We are pleased that management has listened and we have reached a fair compromise."

The company confirmed on Tuesday that an agreement had been brokered, including a 12% wage increase over the next two years and adjustments to overtime compensation. “We value our workforce and are committed to constructive dialogue,” a Jinxiang spokesperson said. “Production lines have restarted, and we are working to fulfill back orders as quickly as possible.”

Industry analysts noted the strike’s potential to expose vulnerabilities in the region’s industrial supply chain. "The walkout at Jinxiang highlights the growing importance of labor relations in China’s intermediate goods sector," said Xu Wei, an analyst at Huadong Industrial Research. "Supply interruptions, even for a week, can have a ripple effect on contractual obligations and delivery schedules."

The Shandong Industrial Association welcomed the resolution of the dispute. “We are relieved to see operations resume at one of our key members,” said association secretary Zhang Min. “This outcome demonstrates the value of dialogue between labor and management.”

Jinxiang Industrial Materials said that normal operations have resumed at all affected facilities and that it is coordinating closely with customers to minimize further delays.
